routes.label: Locate the face centers, prove disjointness and use sphere volume ratios

changes.rationale: Regular tetrahedron vertices (+,+,+),(+,-,-),(-,+,-),(-,-,+) in coordinates +/-1 give R=sqrt(3), face distance r=1/sqrt(3). An exterior face-tangent sphere center is (r+rho)n. All four are internally tangent to the big sphere and externally tangent to the central sphere, so disjoint interiors give uniform volume ratio 5*(r/R)^3=5/27. Internal tangency is derived by the radial maximum, not imported from an external-tangency-only node.

Therefore the difference from 3/4 is (1/2-cos(x-y))*(1/2+cos(x+y)). Monotonic sine on its principal interval and cofunction identities justify the cosine thresholds; this is not inferred from a sketch. Removing two triangles of leg pi/6 and one of leg pi/3 from area pi^2/4 gives pi^2/6.
